title_en: Ying Gaofeng v. Jiameide (Shanghai) Trading Co., Ltd. and Chen Huimei — other contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: I. In an action for disregard of corporate personality of a one-person company, a distinction should be made based on the grounds on which the creditor as plaintiff brings the lawsuit. If the creditor sues the shareholder for joint and several liability for the company's debts on the ground that the shareholder and the company have commingled their assets, the burden of proof shall be reversed, and the defendant shareholder shall bear the burden of proving that there is no commingling between his personal property and the company's property. In other circumstances, the general principle for allocation of the burden of proof for disregard of corporate personality of a limited liability company shall be followed, i.e., the compromise principle for allocation of the burden of proof.
keywords_en: civil; contract dispute; one-person company corporate personality denial; first instance; basic people's court; Shanghai; natural person; legal person; company law; burden of proof for commingling of assets between one-person company and its shareholder; whether conditions for rescission of investment contract are fulfilled; partially upheld; investment contract; one-person company; commingling of assets; audit report; corporate personality denial; Chen Huimei — other contract dispute
full_text_en:
Ying Gaofeng v. Jiameide (Shanghai) Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd. and Chen Huimei — dispute over other contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. In a lawsuit for piercing the corporate veil of a one-person limited liability company, the cause of action on which the creditor as plaintiff bases its claim shall be distinguished. Where the creditor claims that the shareholder of a one-person company and the company have commingled assets and seeks to hold the shareholder jointly and severally liable for the company's debts, the burden of proof shall be reversed, and the defendant shareholder shall bear the burden of proving that there is no commingling between his or her personal property and the company's property. In other circumstances, the general principle for allocating the burden of proof in actions for piercing the corporate veil of a limited liability company shall apply, namely, the principle of compromise in the allocation of the burden of proof.

II. Whether the property of a one-person company is commingled with the shareholder's personal property shall be determined by conducting a comprehensive review of whether the company has established an independent and standardized financial system, whether financial payments are clear, and whether it has an independent business premises.

Plaintiff: Ying Gaofeng, male, 37 years old, of Han ethnicity, residing in Yongkang City, Zhejiang Province.

Defendant: Jiameide (Shanghai) Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xianxia Road, Changning District, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Chen Huimei, Executive Director of the Company.

Defendant: Chen Huimei, female, 55 years old, a resident of the Taiwan region, residing in Changning District, Shanghai.

The plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, filed an action with the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants, Jiameide (Shanghai) Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jiameide Company") and Chen Huimei, concerning a dispute over other contracts.

The plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, alleged: The defendant, Jiameide Company, is a wholly owned enterprise operated by the defendant, Chen Huimei. On August 2, 2012, the plaintiff, the two defendants, and a third party, Chen Zhuojian (Chen Huimei's husband), entered into an "Investment Contract" stipulating that Ying Gaofeng would invest in Jiameide Company and hold equity in the Company. Due to the short negotiation period and incomplete financial materials provided by the two defendants at the time of signing, the contract specifically provided: within three months after signing, if Ying Gaofeng had different opinions on the financial statements and operational statements provided by the two defendants before or after signing, or if the two defendants breached the contract, Ying Gaofeng had the right to unilaterally terminate the investment agreement by written notice, and Jiameide Company must unconditionally refund the funds already invested by Ying Gaofeng. The contract further stipulated that Chen Zhuojian would fully transfer to Jiameide Company the brand rights of "Amada" in the Hong Kong and Macau regions of China, and that all business of the third party, Shanghai Jundai Daily Gift Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jundai Company"), would be transferred to Jiameide Company. After the contract was signed, Ying Gaofeng paid RMB 2,081,633 to Jiameide Company and simultaneously entrusted an accounting firm to audit the financial materials supplemented by the two defendants after signing. The audit results showed that the financial and asset conditions of Jiameide Company were seriously inconsistent with the financial data informed by the two defendants before signing, and that the "Amada" brand under Chen Zhuojian's name and the business of Jundai Company had not been transferred to Jiameide Company as agreed. Based on this, Ying Gaofeng notified the two defendants to terminate the "Investment Contract" in accordance with the agreement. The two defendants agreed to refund RMB 400,000 and made a statement regarding the repayment of the remaining amount of more than RMB 1,600,000. However, thereafter, Ying Gaofeng made repeated telephone calls and sent correspondence, but the two defendants refused to refund the remaining balance. Ying Gaofeng thus filed this action, requesting the court to: 1. Order Jiameide Company to refund the investment funds of RMB 1,681,633; 2. Order Jiameide Company to pay interest losses on the above investment funds, calculated at the bank's loan interest rate for the same period from May 30, 2013, to the date of entry into effect of the judgment; 3. Order Chen Huimei to assume joint and several liability for the above payment obligations.

The defendant, Jiameide Company, argued in defense: According to the terms of the "Investment Contract," the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, had completed his capital contribution to Jiameide Company. His current request to withdraw the capital contribution based on Article 8 of the contract violates the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and should be null and void. Ying Gaofeng's demand to withdraw the capital contribution without any consultation with Jiameide Company lacks legal basis. Moreover, the audit report submitted by Ying Gaofeng was commissioned by a third party, Shanghai Oudelong International Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Oudelong Company"), from an accounting firm and is irrelevant to this case. Ying Gaofeng has no evidence to show any difference in the financial condition and operational statements of Jiameide Company before and after signing the contract. Therefore, Ying Gaofeng's request to withdraw the capital contribution is factually unfounded.

The defendant, Chen Huimei, argued in defense: Among the investment funds paid by the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, under the contract, except for the RMB 400,000 already refunded to Ying Gaofeng, the remainder was used for the operation of the defendant, Jiameide Company. Moreover, Chen Huimei's signature on the "Investment Contract" was merely authorized by Jiameide Company. She is not a party to this case and should not assume joint and several liability for Jiameide Company's debts.

The Changning District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts at first instance:

The defendant, Jiameide Company, was established on August 9, 2006. The Company's current registered capital is RMB 1,000,000, and the paid-in capital is RMB 1,000,000. The company type is a limited liability company (sole proprietorship by a natural person from Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Macau), and both the shareholder and the legal representative are Chen Huimei.

On August 2, 2012, the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, Jiameide Company, and the third party, Chen Zhuojian, signed the "Investment Contract," in which the parties agreed: Ying Gaofeng would invest in Jiameide Company to maximize the development of its existing operating brands and channels. The total investment amount was RMB 10,000,000, and Ying Gaofeng would acquire 51% of the shares of Jiameide Company. Ying Gaofeng's capital contributions would be paid in installments: the first tranche of RMB 2,000,000 would be remitted to a designated account within three days from the date of signing; the second tranche of RMB 2,000,000 would be remitted to a designated account within ninety days from the date of signing; the remaining RMB 6,000,000 would be remitted to a designated account within eighteen months after signing, according to the operational needs and instructions of Jiameide Company. Jiameide Company agreed that Ying Gaofeng would be entitled to exercise shareholder rights immediately after the first remittance of RMB 2,000,000 to the designated account. Within three months after signing, if Ying Gaofeng had different opinions on the financial statements and operational statements provided by Jiameide Company before or after signing, and the parties could not reach a consensus through coordination, or if Jiameide Company breached the terms of the contract, Ying Gaofeng reserved the right to revoke this investment contract. If Ying Gaofeng notified the Company in writing to revoke the contract, the Company agreed unconditionally to remit the funds deposited by Ying Gaofeng into the account to a bank account designated by Ying Gaofeng within sixty days after Ying Gaofeng's notice, and to terminate the contract. The agreement further stipulated: Within sixty days after Ying Gaofeng signed the contract with Jiameide Company, Chen Zhuojian would fully transfer the ownership of the "Amada" brand in the Hong Kong and Macau regions of China to Jiameide Company, and Jiameide Company would exclusively own all rights to the brand in those regions. All business of Jundai Company would be transferred to Jiameide Company. The financial receipts and payments of Jiameide Company would be executed only after being jointly signed and sealed by Ying Gaofeng and the Company. Ying Gaofeng had the right to confirm in advance before signing all cooperation documents of the Company's shareholders and the Company's agency contracts. Before the parties signed the above "Investment Contract," a third party, Zhang Ziliang, participated in the negotiations and had sent draft contract texts to Chen Zhuojian and Chen Huimei.

On August 6, 2012, the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, paid investment funds of RMB 2,081,633 to the defendant, Jiameide Company.

Between August and September 2012, the third party, Zhang Ziliang, went to the defendant, Jiameide Company, signed payment requisition forms, payment notices, and payment vouchers, and at one time held the Company's U-shield. Zhang Ziliang returned the U-shield to the defendant, Chen Huimei.

On September 29, 2012, the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, entrusted a third party, Yu Xincun, to send an email to the defendants, Chen Huimei and Chen Zhuojian, stating: "This week, the audit at your company was completed. Based on the inventory count of your company, the lack of financial statements and accounting vouchers, discrepancies in the figures, and your own lack of understanding of the financial situation, we are deeply concerned about this investment case. After internal discussions, we have decided to terminate this contract and request a refund of the remitted RMB 2,081,633 according to the contract. Please confirm the repayment time and method as soon as possible."

On October 22, 2012, Shanghai Shenzhou Datong Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., upon the entrustment of the third party, Oudelong Company, issued a "Special Audit Report" after auditing the consolidated internal management financial statements of the defendant, Jiameide Company, and Jundai Company for the period of January to August 2012. The report found: The book value of Jiameide Company's main business revenue was RMB 1,072,883.46, and the book value of Jundai Company's main business revenue was RMB 3,211,001.43; however, the total amount on the consolidated profit statement differed from the sum of the book values of the two companies by RMB 2,909,993.21. The book value of Jiameide Company's main business cost was RMB 853,941.12, and the book value of Jundai Company's main business cost was RMB 2,208,777.86; however, the total on the consolidated profit statement differed from the sum of the book values of the two companies by RMB 586,845.18. According to the consolidated balance sheet, the retained earnings at the beginning of the period were RMB 7,632,686.49, plus the net profit for the current period of RMB 366,605.96, resulting in retained earnings at the end of the period of RMB 7,999,292.45; however, the retained earnings at the end of the period shown on the consolidated balance sheet were RMB 6,110,244.03, a difference of RMB 1,889,048.42 between the two figures. The report also noted that it was for the evaluation and analysis of the consolidated internal management financial statements of Jiameide Company and Jundai Company by the client, Oudelong Company, only, and not for other purposes.

On November 21, 2012, the defendant, Chen Huimei, sent an email to Yu Xincun, stating: "Regarding the share withdrawal mechanism, we very much respect your choice. Our party has remitted RMB 400,000 back on Friday; this is the remaining cash from the investment amount. Goods worth RMB 500,000 will be listed on Monday; the investment amount has been used to pay for the goods, so we can only return the goods. As for the remaining RMB 1,100,000, which has been used to pay various expenses, we can only reserve 5% of the shares for your party."

On the same day, an agricultural bank account of the third party, Hu Huajing, received a payment of RMB 400,000 from the defendant, Jiameide Company, with the transaction purpose stated as "payment for goods." The plaintiff and the defendants jointly confirmed that this payment was the investment funds refunded by Jiameide Company to the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng.

On November 28, 2012, the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, sent a certified mail letter to the defendants, Jiameide Company and Chen Zhuojian, requesting the return of the remaining RMB 1,680,000 within one week.

On December 4, 2012, the defendant, Jiameide Company, sent a reply letter to the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, arguing that Ying Gaofeng had never consulted or communicated with the Company before sending a letter requesting the revocation of the "Investment Contract" and the return of the remaining RMB 1,680,000, which was inconsistent with the true intent and purpose of the contract. According to the net value calculated by the accountants and after deducting expenses for decoration, purchases, rent, payment for goods, equipment purchases, wages, and other related costs during the investment period from the investment funds of RMB 2,080,000 paid by Ying Gaofeng, the Company had made its best efforts to remit RMB 400,000 to the account designated by Ying Gaofeng, and there was no remaining RMB 1,680,000 to be returned. Ying Gaofeng's demand lacked any contractual or legal basis and was contrary to good faith and fairness. On December 6, 2012, the defendant, Chen Huimei, sent an email responding to the certified mail letter, stating that she had been negotiating the share withdrawal mechanism with Ying Gaofeng, but Ying Gaofeng had not agreed. She requested that Ying Gaofeng's accountant provide a calculation method.

On December 13, 2012, the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, entrusted a lawyer to send a lawyer's letter to the defendant, Jiameide Company, stating that Ying Gaofeng disagreed with the reply letter sent by the Company on December 4 of the same year and again demanded the return of the investment funds.

It was also found that between August 2012 and June 2013, the defendant, Jiameide Company, made multiple external payments, including freight, agency fees, storage fees, service fees, taxes, decoration fees, rent, property management fees, and monthly telephone rental fees, totaling more than RMB 3,700,000.

It was further found that Jundai Company was a limited liability company (domestic joint venture), established on June 28, 2004, with registered capital and paid-in capital both of RMB 500,000. Its legal representative was Ma Jianru, and its shareholders were Ma Jianru and Tao Weifeng.

During the first instance trial, the defendant, Jiameide Company, confirmed that it had only a trading partnership with Jundai Company and that there was no affiliation between the two companies. The defendants, Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei, confirmed that the ownership of the "Amada" brand and the business of Jundai Company had not been transferred to Jiameide Company to date. Additionally, regarding Jiameide Company's defense that it had used the investment funds paid by the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, for the Company's operations, the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai sought Jiameide Company's opinion on whether an audit was necessary for this purpose. The Court explained to Jiameide Company the burden of proof it bore and the possible consequences of not conducting an audit, but Jiameide Company insisted on not conducting an audit.

The Changning District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance:

The plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, the defendant, Jiameide Company, and the third party, Chen Zhuojian, agreed that Ying Gaofeng would invest in Jiameide Company to acquire 51% of the shares of the Company; Chen Zhuojian would transfer the ownership of the "Amada" brand owned by him to Jiameide Company, and Jundai Company would transfer its business to Jiameide Company. It can be seen that Ying Gaofeng's signing of the "Investment Contract" and payment of investment funds to Jiameide Company were not merely for the purpose of acquiring shares in Jiameide Company, but were an investment decision based on the expectation that Jiameide Company could acquire the ownership of the "Amada" brand and the business of Jundai Company and had a good development prospect. Since the above "Investment Contract" was the true intention of the parties and did not violate the mandatory laws and regulations of China, it was legal and valid, and all parties should strictly perform it. The plaintiff and the defendants now have the following disputed issues regarding the above "Investment Contract": 1. Whether Jiameide Company should refund the balance of Ying Gaofeng's investment funds; 2. Whether the defendant, Chen Huimei, should assume joint and several liability for Jiameide Company's repayment obligation. In this regard, the Court's findings are as follows:

Regarding the first disputed issue, the "Investment Contract" clearly states: Within three months after the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, signed the contract with the defendant, Jiameide Company, if Ying Gaofeng had different opinions on the financial statements and operational statements provided by Jiameide Company before or after signing, and the parties could not reach a consensus through coordination, or if Jiameide Company breached the terms of the contract, Ying Gaofeng reserved the right to revoke the "Investment Contract." If Ying Gaofeng notified Jiameide Company in writing to revoke the contract, Jiameide Company agreed unconditionally to remit the funds deposited by Ying Gaofeng into its account to a bank account designated by Ying Gaofeng within sixty days after Ying Gaofeng's notice, and to terminate the "Investment Contract." According to the facts found by the Court, it can be determined that the defendant, Chen Huimei, had provided Ying Gaofeng with the relevant statements of Jiameide Company. Although Ying Gaofeng was unable to apply for an audit of these statements by an auditing institution in his own name, the "Audit Report" for which Oudelong Company was the applicant had already pointed out problems in the statements, which were beyond doubt. Based on this, Ying Gaofeng proposed to Jiameide Company to terminate the "Investment Contract" and demanded the return of the investment funds. This act did not violate the terms of the "Investment Contract." Subsequently, Chen Huimei sent an email to Ying Gaofeng, without denying or objecting to the problems pointed out by Ying Gaofeng and the demand to terminate the "Investment Contract." From this, it can be determined that Ying Gaofeng and Jiameide Company had reached a mutual agreement to terminate the "Investment Contract." Jiameide Company argued in defense that Ying Gaofeng's request to withdraw the capital contribution violated the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and should be null and void. The Court held that the "Investment Contract" signed by the plaintiff and the defendant involved equity, brand ownership, business transfer, etc., and was not limited to capital contribution to the Company. When Ying Gaofeng proposed to terminate the contract to Jiameide Company in September 2012, neither party had completed the procedures for changing the company registration, and Ying Gaofeng had not yet become a shareholder of Jiameide Company. Therefore, Ying Gaofeng's request for the return of the investment funds was not contrary to law, and Jiameide Company's defense argument was difficult to sustain.

Regarding the amount of the refund of investment funds, the defendant, Chen Huimei, had sent an email to the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, expressing agreement to refund RMB 400,000 in cash, goods worth RMB 500,000, and to offset the remaining RMB 1,100,000 with 5% of the shares. From this, it can be seen that the defendant, Jiameide Company, did not dispute the amount of the investment funds to be refunded to Ying Gaofeng; it merely put forward its own opinion on whether to refund the full amount in cash or offset part of the amount with goods or shares, and thus a dispute arose with Ying Gaofeng. Since Ying Gaofeng did not accept Jiameide Company's above opinion, and the "Investment Contract" did not provide that after termination of the contract, Jiameide Company could offset the refundable investment funds with goods, shares, etc., Jiameide Company's above request was merely its unilateral expression of intent, lacking basis and difficult to sustain. Moreover, after the termination of the "Investment Contract," Ying Gaofeng would no longer invest in Jiameide Company and would certainly not become a shareholder of the Company. Jiameide Company's request to offset the refundable investment funds with company shares clearly contradicted the original intention of the parties and was not enforceable. In summary, Jiameide Company should refund Ying Gaofeng's investment funds.

Regarding the amount of the refund of investment funds, the defendant, Jiameide Company, argued in defense that, except for the RMB 400,000 already refunded to the plaintiff, Ying Gaofeng, the remaining funds had been used for the Company's operations. However, it only provided various payment vouchers of Jiameide Company for the period from August 2012 to June 2013. These vouchers only reflected the Company's income and expenditure details and failed to prove whether the expenditures derived from the plaintiff's investment funds. During the evidence exchange, the Court inquired about the use of the investment funds paid by Ying Gaofeng from the witness Wu Huiyu. Wu Huiyu answered that the investment funds paid by Ying Gaofeng and other funds of Jiameide Company should have been used together, but since the witness was not responsible for the bookkeeping, the specific situation was unclear. In summary, the use of the investment funds and the source of the expenditures of Jiameide Company could only be ascertained through an audit by a professional institution, combining the Company's financial accounts and relevant payment vouchers and documents. However, after the Court's explanation, Jiameide Company insisted on not conducting an audit. Therefore, the existing evidence alone could hardly prove its defense argument, and the adverse consequences arising therefrom should be borne by Jiameide Company itself. Furthermore, even if Jiameide Company's defense argument that it had used Ying Gaofeng's investment funds for its operations was valid, since Ying Gaofeng had already proposed via email on September 29, 2012, to Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei to terminate the "Investment Contract" and demanded the return of the investment funds, Jiameide Company's subsequent unauthorized decision to use the investment funds without Ying Gaofeng's permission violated the terms of the "Investment Contract." In summary, Jiameide Company should refund the balance of RMB 1,681,633 of Ying Gaofeng's investment funds. Jiameide Company's failure to refund the above investment funds in a timely manner has already caused losses to Ying Gaofeng. Ying Gaofeng's request for Jiameide Company to pay interest losses on the overdue repayment from the date of filing the case is legally sound and well-founded and should be supported.

Regarding the second issue in dispute, Defendant Jiameide Company is a one-person limited liability company invested in by Defendant Chen Huimei. According to Article 63 of the Company Law of the PRC, where the shareholder of a one-person limited liability company cannot prove that the company's property is independent from the shareholder's own property, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts. Chen Huimei, as the shareholder of Jiameide Company, represented Jiameide Company in negotiating the investment matters with Plaintiff Ying Gaofeng, signed the "Investment Contract," and also sent emails on behalf of Jiameide Company to Ying Gaofeng regarding the issue of whether the investment funds should be returned. The expression of intent between Chen Huimei and Jiameide Company was consistent, not independent of each other. Furthermore, as the sole shareholder of Jiameide Company, Chen Huimei failed to provide evidence to the court proving that Jiameide Company's property was independent from her personal property. Moreover, as Jiameide Company insisted on not undergoing an audit, it was impossible to prove that the investment funds delivered by Ying Gaofeng had been used for Jiameide Company and had not been used for other purposes. In conclusion, to prevent the sole shareholder of a one-person company from abusing the independent legal personality of the company and to enhance the protection of the company's creditors, Ying Gaofeng's claim requesting Chen Huimei to bear joint and several liability for the debts of Jiameide Company should be granted.

Accordingly, the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Article 93, Paragraph 2 and Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Articles 35 and 63 of the Company Law of the PRC, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, rendered the following judgment on May 30, 2014:

1. Defendant Jiameide Company shall, within ten days of this judgment taking effect, refund to Plaintiff Ying Gaofeng the investment capital of RMB 1,681,633;

2. Defendant Jiameide Company shall, within ten days of this judgment taking effect, compensate Plaintiff Ying Gaofeng for the interest loss on the overdue refund of the investment capital, calculated based on the principal of RMB 1,681,633 from May 30, 2013 to the date this judgment takes effect, at the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and term issued by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period;

3. Defendant Chen Huimei shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of Defendant Jiameide Company under items 1 and 2 of the above judgment.

Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal with the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei appealed, arguing: 1. The special audit report recognized by the first-instance court was commissioned by Oudelun Company, and one part of the audit content involved Jundai Company, but it did not explain the relationship between Oudelun Company and Jundai Company and this case. The Respondent Ying Gaofeng, without requesting Jiameide Company to provide financial statements, hastily remitted the funds and sent personnel to Jiameide Company, and within less than 60 days, based on an invalid audit report, demanded termination of the contract. The investment risk of Ying Gaofeng should be borne by himself. 2. Chen Huimei should not be personally liable. The disputed "Investment Contract" had nothing to do with Chen Huimei personally; Chen Huimei only signed the contract in her capacity as the legal representative of Jiameide Company. The funds from Ying Gaofeng were remitted into Jiameide Company's account, not Chen Huimei's personal account, and during the trial of this case, no evidence was found of any economic dealings between Chen Huimei personally and Jiameide Company. Accordingly, they requested the revocation of the original judgment and a revised judgment ordering Jiameide Company to return the remaining residual value of Ying Gaofeng's investment funds after they were contributed to the company, and that Chen Huimei should not bear joint and several liability.

The Respondent Ying Gaofeng argued in defense that the appeal grounds of Appellants Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei lacked factual and legal basis, and therefore requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon trial at second instance, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

During the second instance, the two appellants submitted the following evidence: the "Financial Statements and Audit Reports" for the years 2011 to 2013, the "Audit Report on Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Statement" for 2011, and the "Audit Report on Confirmation of Foreign Investor's Rights and Interests for Foreign-Invested Enterprises" for 2012 and 2013, intending to prove that Appellant Jiameide Company had independent financial accounts and that there was no commingling of property with Appellant Chen Huimei individually. Upon examination, the Respondent Ying Gaofeng argued that these reports were prepared based on fixed items in financial reports and could not prove the absence of property commingling between Jiameide Company and Chen Huimei personally. Furthermore, the 2013 report stated that Jiameide Company had no undisclosed pending litigation, but this dispute had been ongoing since June 2013, so he did not recognize the truthfulness of the report's content.

During the second instance, the Respondent Ying Gaofeng submitted the corporate archive information of Jundai Limited Company registered in Taiwan, intending to prove that the Shanghai Jundai Company was actually controlled by Appellant Chen Huimei, and that Chen Huimei used the Shanghai Jundai Company to freely control and transfer the assets of Appellant Jiameide Company for her own use. Upon examination, the two appellants did not object to the authenticity of the above evidence but argued that the Shanghai Jundai Company was not completely controlled by Jiameide Company.

Upon review, the court found that the financial reports submitted by the two appellants had been presented with originals, their authenticity could be confirmed, and they were relevant to the dispute in this case; therefore, the court admitted them according to law. The enterprise information of Jundai Limited Company registered in Taiwan submitted by Respondent Ying Gaofeng was not directly related to the dispute in this case, as that company was not the investing company of Shanghai Jundai Company, and therefore it was not admitted.

The court accordingly found additional facts: Between 2011 and 2013, Appellant Jiameide Company commissioned relevant accounting firms to audit and review the company's financial statements, respectively. The "Financial Statements and Audit Reports" for 2011 to 2013 confirmed that the financial statements of Jiameide Company were prepared in all material respects in accordance with the accounting standards for small enterprises and fairly presented the financial position, operating results, and cash flows of Jiameide Company. The "Audit Report on Confirmation of Foreign Investor's Rights and Interests for Foreign-Invested Enterprises" for 2012 and 2013 and the "Audit Report on Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Statement" for 2011 confirmed that the preparation of Jiameide Company's foreign investor's rights and interests confirmation statements and foreign exchange receipts and payments statements was in all material respects in compliance with the relevant provisions of the state on foreign exchange administration.

During the second instance, the two appellants stated that Appellant Jiameide Company had actual control over Jundai Company, and therefore it could guarantee that all of Jundai Company's business would be transferred to Jiameide Company in accordance with the "Investment Contract".

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

The issues in dispute at second instance are: 1. After the termination of the investment contract, should Appellant Jiameide Company refund the full amount of Respondent Ying Gaofeng's investment capital, or refund based on the remaining residual value of the investment capital? 2. Should Appellant Chen Huimei bear joint and several liability for the refund of the investment capital?

First, regarding the issue of how Appellant Jiameide Company should refund the investment capital. The court held that, according to the "Investment Contract", within three months after signing, if Respondent Ying Gaofeng had different opinions on the financial statements and operating statements of Jiameide Company, and the parties could not reach a consensus through negotiation, Ying Gaofeng had the right to revoke the investment contract, and Jiameide Company agreed to unconditionally refund Ying Gaofeng's investment funds and terminate this contract. During the performance of the contract, Ying Gaofeng notified Jiameide Company on September 29, 2012 to terminate the investment contract and demanded the return of the full investment amount. Appellant Chen Huimei, on behalf of Jiameide Company, replied on November 21 of the same year, stating that she respected Ying Gaofeng's choice, had remitted RMB 400,000 to Ying Gaofeng, and at the same time stated that the remaining investment funds had been used to pay for goods and various expenses. It can be seen from this that Ying Gaofeng's claim for the return of the full investment amount from Jiameide Company was in line with the parties' contractual agreement. After Ying Gaofeng notified the termination of the investment contract, Jiameide Company did not object to the full refund of the investment amount. The fact of whether the investment funds had already been used for operations and whether Jiameide Company was unable to repay could not alter the parties' contractual agreement, nor could it exempt Jiameide Company from its repayment obligation. This ground of appeal by Jiameide Company could not stand. The original judgment ordering Jiameide Company to bear the full repayment obligation was correct and should be upheld.

Second, regarding the issue of whether Appellant Chen Huimei should personally bear joint and several liability for repayment. The court held that, according to Article 63 of the Company Law of the PRC, where the shareholder of a one-person limited liability company cannot prove that the company's property is independent from the shareholder's own property, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts. This legal provision requires the shareholder of a one-person limited liability company to strictly separate the company's property from personal finances, and the shareholder bears the burden of proof on whether their personal property is separate from the company's property. In this case, Chen Huimei provided relevant audit reports of Appellant Jiameide Company, which could reflect that Jiameide Company had an independent and complete financial system, the relevant financial statements complied with accounting standards and national foreign exchange administration regulations, and there were no signs of commingling of company property with the shareholder's personal property. This could basically reflect the fact that Jiameide Company's property was separate from Chen Huimei's personal property. Ying Gaofeng argued that the above evidence was insufficient to prove that there was no commingling of Jiameide Company's property with Chen Huimei's personal property and raised the following objections: the audit report did not reflect the litigation status of this case; the bank receipts and payments report provided by Jiameide Company in the first instance showed that, only one week after Ying Gaofeng's investment, Jiameide Company transferred over RMB 960,000 to Jundai Company, including payment of Jundai Company's employee salaries, etc. The court held that the provision of Article 64 of the Company Law of the PRC is intended to restrict shareholders of one-person limited liability companies from using means such as commingling company property with personal property to evade debts and harm the interests of the company's creditors. Therefore, the prerequisite for a shareholder to bear joint and several liability for the company's debts is that the shareholder's personal property is commingled with the company's property. However, based on the evidence currently available in this case, after Jiameide Company received Ying Gaofeng's investment funds, although part of them was used to pay the wages and goods expenses of Jundai Company's employees, etc., according to the parties' investment contract, after Ying Gaofeng's investment, all of Jundai Company's business would be transferred to Jiameide Company. Therefore, the business expenditures of Jundai Company were directly related to Ying Gaofeng's investment project; these expenditures were all used for Jundai Company's business expenses, and there was no record of funds being transferred into Chen Huimei's personal account. Furthermore, whether the audit report recorded the litigation of this case was unrelated to the issue of property commingling. Therefore, the objections raised by Ying Gaofeng could not reflect signs of commingling of Jiameide Company's property with Chen Huimei's personal property and were insufficient to negate the appellants' evidence. Chen Huimei's ground of appeal was valid. The first-instance judgment ordering Chen Huimei to bear joint and several liability for the debts of Jiameide Company was improper and should be corrected according to law.

In summary, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on October 27, 2014:

1. Affirm items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (2013) Chang Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. S829 of the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai;

2. Reverse item 3 of the civil judgment (2013) Chang Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. S829 of the Changning District People's Court of Shanghai;

3. Dismiss Ying Gaofeng's remaining claims.

This judgment is final.
